Aircraft on final approach; under tower control; was overflown by aircraft operating out of nearby class b airspace. Class b approach controller did not advise tower of traffic.

Pf; FO; inexperienced in aircraft; inadvertently extended leading edge devices thinking he was extending speed brakes causing aircraft damage due to high speed leading edge device deployment.

Land without clearance. Distractions from tcasii alert on final plus flocks of birds contributed to the FLC forgetting to switch frequency to tower.

Heli pilot for gov office complaint regarding frequency interference of detroit tower frequency.

A part 135 cargo pilot reports following a controller's clearance to taxi into position and hold; but then having to hold on the runway for over 2 minutes; while a twin landed over the top of his aircraft. The atct lcl controller then clred the reporter for takeoff.

The FLC of an E120 shut down the #1 engine after noting an 'exceedingly high' oil pressure indication. The FLC then requested ATC assistance and returned to their origination airport; which was 100 NM away.

During climb; a B727 FLC noticed a fuel sys problem after a fuel imbal btwn the #1 and #3 tanks had developed. It was determined that there were approx 18000 lbs of unusable fuel onboard; so the flight diverted. The mech's report indicates that prior to departure he had inadvertently secured the #1 xfeed valve in the open position as opposed to the #3 valve; that was inop and failed in the closed position.
An acr B747 mech and his maintenance control supvr apparently disagree on the interp of the MEL. Aircraft equip problem AFT cargo lateral guides inop electrically.
An acr mlg had to return land with an aircraft equip problem air conditioning pack failure. Emer declared.

A commuter FLC took evasive action to avoid an aircraft after entering VMC from IMC. The crew had been deviating around weather and was alerted by the approach controller who also issued a heading change.

A corp jet FLC overshot their assigned alt during departure. The controller advised of the traffic conflict with 2 A10's in formation flight. One of the A10's was sighted at the alt that the FLC had been assigned.

A captain reports confusion with ATC instructions during touch- and-go landings while on a demo flight. The FLC was told to discontinue a short approach for no apparent reason and then corrected with a turn the opposite direction; when they were entering the pattern for the newly assigned runway.
The copilot of a BE9F applied brakes during landing and blew the tires on the right main landing gear. The runway was closed while the tires were replaced.
Flc received GPWS warnings while on the loc DME approach with pull-ups and terrain calls. Aircraft radar altimeter showed 1200 ft at closest point.
An acr mlg clbed to avoid an acr MD11. Tcasii commanded the climb. The mlg was lining up for sfo; the MD11 was maneuvering for sjc.

An acr captain reports landing without a clearance. The FO discovered that the radio was still tuned to the approach controller's frequency when the aircraft was 50 ft AGL. The FO then contacted the tower; and through later review with the tower supvr; the FLC was told that the controller had clred them to land.

While taxiing out; a flight attendant came running up the aisle; unlocked the cockpit door; and said there was a loud boom in the aircraft. At the same time the interphone from the AFT cabin flight attendants alerted pilots the AFT cabin was filling with smoke and suggested evacing the aircraft. The aircraft was evaced in less than a min and the emer crash equip was called. Appropriate emer and evac procedures were accomplished. There was no fire and no one was injured.
The pilot of a home-built baby ace GND looped; left the runway; and nosed over. He was not injured.

Commuter aircraft overloaded and out of center of gravity. 3 legs flown without inspection of aircraft.

An acr B727 PIC voices his concerns with continuing his flight without entering the inop engine start valve in the logbook and having maintenance sign it off.

An acr light responded to a tcasii command and an ARTCC command to avoid ltss with another aircraft.

Altdev alt XING restr not met undershot in climb. Overwater op; wdb aircraft delayed climb to next alt. Controller has short talk with crew.
An acr FLC finds that their contract fueler is untrained in refueling with fuel gauges inop. Had to be aided by an airline operations agent who had 'done it a long time ago.'
Corp jet suffers a heading track dev in prox of tstm activity after their weather radar experiences a malfunction.
Low time pvt pilot makes an early descent prior to faf on approach procedure VOR DME approach.

Flc flew wrong SID after takeoff. No mention was made by the tower or departure controller to FLC concerning the dev. Reporter saw departing aircraft and then realized they were on the wrong SID. Apparent loss of separation; but ATC was unconcerned.
Takeoff abort due to flaps not in position. Warning horn alerted FLC.
Pilot allowed aircraft on autoplt to drift off airway. Approach controller intervened with advisory.

Artcc radar controller assigned an alt and; as FLC clbed; controller questioned their alt. When controller realized he had made an error he apologized and issued the correct alt clearance.
After parking; reporter was inspected by an FAA inspector who found cargo had come loose and some other cargo not secured properly.

Aircraft was parked and FLC departed. Later FLC received call that aircraft had been damaged by hitting belt loader. Reporter captain taxied under marshaller guidance at night. It was possible that the belt loader driver hit the aircraft.
With a rerte and alt change at the same time; FLC forgot to start descent until asked by ATC.

Late holding instructions and FLC rushed to insert it in FMS. Reporter captain inadvertently entered right turn pattern and the depicted pattern is left turns. After first turn ATC questioned the direction of their turn and corrected the pattern.

text: An nmac occurred when a departure and a missed approach occupied the same airspace simultaneously. The two procedures have a built-in conflict when a missed approach is executed and departure either proceeds or immediately follows the missed approach.
Altdev. Descent below clred alt. Miscom and misunderstanding within FLC about alt clearance. Fatigue a factor.

Aircraft equip problem. Borescope plug missing. Reporter mech; unfamiliar with aircraft type; was assigned job of installing borescope plugs. Reporter says that the number of plugs he installed coincided with the amount shown on the job card. After aircraft was in flight they had intermittent fire warnings and on post flight inspection a borescope plug missing.

Atc approach controller advised the FLC of an mlg that they were not indicating assigned alt by 500 ft too low. Flc's 3 altimeters all showed the correct assigned alt and set to the current altimeter setting.

An air taxi jet captain reports that a las approach controller's vector clearance placed their aircraft on a collision course with an MD80. The MD80 FLC took evasive action; dsnding and passing approx 500 ft below them.
Artcc radar controller was vectoring 2 acr aircraft for separation and dsnding one at the same time. Reporter controller misjudged the spacing and the aircraft ended up with ltss.

Flc of a beechcraft 100; king air; lost all electrical sys; including the battery source; in IMC due to mismgmnt of the start engine switches. The crew was able to cancel IFR via a cellular phone through their company.
Flc of an light overshot descent alt causing an ATC alt alert.
Air taxi smt pilot lands gear up.
Nmac btwn an MD88 on final approach and a cessna citation jet overshooting the final approach on a parallel runway.

Flc of an ltt turboprop made a missed approach after the landing gear failed to extend during an inst approach in IMC. The landing gear was subsequently extended manually and an uneventful landing made.
An acr ltt took off at a runway intersection when they needed the full length.
Student of a cessna 172 experienced a partial pwr loss on initial climb after takeoff resulting in returning to land and a 'hard bouncy landing' causing damage to the prop.

While attempting to keep the speed up to follow a jet; a C206 amphibian pilot failed to extend the landing gear. The front seat pax who was also a pilot; was distr looking for traffic and failed to notice. The aircraft was landed gear up; damaging the keel wear strips.
Flc of an mlg diverted to land after cabin attendants and pax were injured by severe turb. Those injured were taken to a hospital for examination. No injuries were considered serious.
B737-500 FLC has problem when company aircraft with similar sounding a/n responds to clearance which was meant for reporter aircraft.

Pilot obtained a ferry permit for his cessna 336 for a ferry flight for repairs and then operated the aircraft without an auth logbook signature required to make the ferry permit effective.
An acr B757 may have missed a frequency change; or they may have been 'forgotten' in the sys.

Flc of an FK100 overshot descent alt during descent due to the captain's misunderstanding of the latest ATC descent instructions resulting in ATC intervention.
Captain of a B747-400 lost control of aircraft for a brief period of time due to severe clear air turb resulting in a net loss of alt of 2000 ft.

Acr mlg has an inflt encounter with tstm activity; asks for assistance in radar vectoring from ATC in prox of warning area.
Emer off airport landing made by pilot in a J3 cub. Aircraft damaged in landing on golf course.

Non adherence to ATC clearance by acr FLC as they attempt to avoid tstm activity by creating a heading track dev.

Nmac by atx pilot with XING same alt traffic in prox of tca b airspace.

Dc10 cargo flight experiences an altdev alt undershot XING restr not met in SID. Departure controller calls for an early turn; placing the aircraft in a no win situation without amended clearance.
A broken connecting rod caused a BE77 pilot to make an emer landing. Dsm tracon gave him the wrong CTAF frequency; so the reporter was met by an aircraft on the runway for takeoff.

Flc of a canadair CL60 making an approach to one airport reported the runway in sight when they were looking at and lined up with another airport runway. The tower controller at the dest airport noticed their mistake and intervened to alert them and bring them back to the correct airport.

text: Flc of a B737 allowed the aircraft to roll over the tow bar after the cgp mech disconnected the tow bar causing damage to the nosewheel strut. The captain inadvertently forgot to set the parking brake before starting the engines.

Flc of an ltt returned to land after 1 engine oil pressure was below acceptable limits and all precautionary chklist procedures would not bring it back. However; since there were no other indications of an actual engine malfunction the engine was left running.

During ILS approach; short final; IMC and night; the autoplt disconnect warning light came one. Reporter thought it had disconnected; but when trying to control the aircraft manually; was unable to gain aileron control before he disconnected manually with the yoke switch and in the meantime had lost 200 ft on the final descent.

Elt (emer locator xmitter) search team in a cessna 172 were exposed to GND searchlights from boats moored near the town over which the search was conducted. It created a blinding view of the team's outside view during the 4- hr search.
Sma spi has circuit breaker on gear pop when trying to extend the landing gear. After several tries he does get 3 green and on landing; gear collapses. Aircraft equip problem landing gear collapse.
An acr B737-400 had to divert land for fuel. Weather factors high alt and high temp at departure airport; cumulo nimbus and arrivals delays at dest.
A commuter FLC failed to put the gear down before ramping an amphibian. The keel strip incurred minor damage. The crew cites fatigue as a factor.
Flc of an mlg returned to the gate for an inspection of the engine after ingesting a plastic bag while holding in a line of aircraft for takeoff.

Flc of an light failed to descend as instructed resulting in not meeting a XING restr. Atc intervened; but it was too late to obtain the correct lower alt by the time the aircraft arrived at the XING fix.

Aircraft equip problem. Generator circuit breaker popped and reporter pilot lost flight information as well as lighting. Reporter still had VHF receiver; but no xmitter. Approach controller provided vectors for a no gyro approach. During approach reporter found generator circuit breaker out and reset; getting back all electrical sys.

Flc of an light failed to hold short and passed the line before the FO stopped the captain from taxiing further and onto the runway causing a landing A300 to touch down near the nose of their aircraft.
So of a B727 failed to follow the manufacturer's fuel management operating procedure for adjusting the fuel tank wt when the fuel in #2 tank exceeds the amount in the #1 or #3 tank.

In quick response to ATC to stop climb and return to an lower alt for traffic; the FLC of a MD80 in doing that; immediately upon rapid throttle retarding hear several 'pop' sounds; similar to an engine compressor stall. However; all engine indications were normal after the incident; so the flight was continued to dest with no problems or noises.
Pilot of an mbb-bk 117 cpr heli failed to clear the heliport boundary fence during landing causing minor damage to the tail stinger and vert stabilizer when they struck the fence.

An MD80 captain reports that he queried a departure controller while on a heading that took the flight away from the intended direction of flight; and still did not receive even an indication of what to expect; nor when to expect on course routing. Tstms were in the path of the intended rte.
A cargo DC8 FLC failed to meet a controller's airspd restr while on the sjc loupe 9 SID. The controller intervened and vectored the crew for traffic.
The pilot of a grob 103 glider returned to land from being on tow for alt when the front canopy opened. However; the pax was able to close it prior to landing.
Altdev. Miscom btwn ATC and FLC. Clearance to 10000 ft and FLC misheard as 11000 ft. Controller intervened when FLC clbed past 10000 ft.
Flc of a B727 overshot climb alt due to the flying FO not having the autoplt pitch control engaged and he was trying to use the autoplt trim to level the aircraft!

During descent; this B727 had all engines flame out. The FLC initially thought it was an electrical emer; but eventually realized the engines were not running. Chklist got the engines back online; but were still not responding properly to throttle movement. Landing was uneventful and everything normal after landing. Incident under investigation by the ntsb.

Flc of a super MD80 stopped before XING a runway to which they were clred to cross when they observed the landing traffic was not going to be able to turn off at the point instructed in their landing clearance.
Flc of a fokker 100 failed to reduce their airspd per arrival STAR fix and subsequently failed to turn to assigned heading at the next STAR fix.

During climb strong odor in cabin; with no warning indications. Aircraft returned to departure airport and during taxi in; it was noticed that the #2 generator was '0' volts and frequencies. No warning lights illuminated at any time. Overwt landing made.
Mlg FLC fails to change altimeter when climbing through FL180. Wrong altimeter setting.
Flc of DC10 fails to meet XING restr when asked to make speed adjustment. Missed XING restr.

During takeoff roll; at approx V1; FLC of a cpr jet observed a vehicle coming toward them on the runway and subsequently go off the side of the runway prior to their aircraft flying over at approx 50 ft. The tower had failed to chk the runway after clring the vehicle on the runway earlier.
An acr DC10 crew overtemped an engine for 3 seconds while fighting for their lives. Weather factors windshear after takeoff.
Lcl controller has 2 aircraft landing on converging runways; gives one aircraft a turn and approval to cross the active converging runway with the other aircraft landing.
An acr B727 crew overshot their climb alt. The reporter complains about no alt capture in this aircraft.

Reporter states that wind gust information is not given unless it is requested. The reporter alleges the tower informed reporter that wind gust information on the atis was adequate and implied that it was not necessary during issuance of requested wind information.

A gov aircraft flew into very bad weather at guatemala city. The FO became incapacitated with fear and confusion. Language barrier. Night op. Designated mountainous terrain. Weather factors turb; tstms and lightning that produced precip static.
A decathlon pilot reports that fuel leaked into his wing and then out wing ventilation vents onto his hangar floor. Error admitted; the fuel cap probably was not properly installed.
An acr B737-200 crew diverted to drop off a violent; intoxicated pax. The fbi later dropped all charges.
Cessna citation (501) has altdev during descent on STAR into lax.

Aircraft equip problem. Landing gear down light. During test flight after previous gear problem; the green gear lights went out on short final. Reporter did a gar and tower fly-by when the lights came back on. Uneventful landing.

After receiving clearance; FLC inserted it into the ins's; but failed to include an intermediate point. Aircraft flew rte as inserted until ATC intervened to advise FLC they were off course. Corrective action followed.
show: 1996-07 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: The nose gear on a CL65 would not retract after takeoff resulting in the FLC's return to the airport. Inspection after landing revealed that the nose gear pin had not been removed.
A hyd sequencing valve failed on a DHC8-300. The nose gear had to be locked down by the emer procedure.

2 flight attendants and 2 pax were injured when an MD11 FLC could not reduce the high descent rate of the aircraft; while on autoplt. When the captain disconnected the autoplt and leveled off; the aircraft had overshot the assigned alt; and occupants in the rear of the aircraft were reported injured during the aircraft's return to clearance alt.
Pa28 pilot departs with 1000 ft and 7 mi but when airborne discovers ceiling is 800 ft. On returning to land enters IMC.
show: 1996-07 · Inflight: VFR In IMC · Initial Climb

text: A B737 FLC encountered windshear immediately after takeoff from phl. A positive rate of climb was achieved and the aircraft departed the windshear environment.
An acr FLC has their B747-200 suddenly pitch up and roll to the right when the #1 ins malfunctions. 1 cabin attendant was injured and the flight was diverted to anc for medical treatment.
show: 1996-07 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Cruise

text: Nmac. Reporter student pilot didn't follow tower instructions 'clred to land #2.' the #1 aircraft turned in front of reporter and a nmac resulted.

Reporter requested a takeoff runway and lined up on it expecting tower to either clear him for takeoff or give further instructions. Tower gave takeoff clearance and coincidental with reporter's takeoff roll was a frequency block from another aircraft. Tower informed reporter that he had taken off on the wrong runway. Miscom btwn tower and pilot.
Aircraft slid off end of grass strip into ditch. Strip was wet and downhill.
show: 1996-07 · Other Runway Or Taxiway Excursion · Landing

text: A grumman ag-cat pilot stalled the aircraft during landing practice; damaging the aircraft. The pilot reports low currency.
A student pilot lost control of the aircraft after landing in gusty conditions. The aircraft left the runway and was damaged when it flipped upside down; on a rough grassy area.
show: 1996-07 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: An acr MD80 got caught in windshear after takeoff at syr. Evasive action windshear escape maneuver. Emer situation not declared.
A C152 crew had to declare an emer due to a partial pwr loss. Their fuel was contaminated with lint.
An acr mdt crew may have landed without clearance.
show: 1996-07 · Procedural: Landing Without Clearance · Initial Approach

text: A C320 corporate pilot loses his right engine for a short time. Starts descent and has a radio communication problem with ATC. Restarts engine and resumes climb.
An acr DC8 freighter crew had a bird strike on final approach to ont. No damage.
A mooney pilot got confused with all of the taxiways at ict and taxied onto the runway without clearance. Error admitted.
An acr EMB120 crew failed to level off at their assigned alt. Altdev. Possible aircraft equip problem autoplt alt capture failed to capture; alt alert not properly armed or inop.

During night; IMC approach and ILS unusable inside the middle marker; reporter faults airport for lack of vasi. With a sloping runway; at night and difficult approach; reporter says it was nearly impossible to gauge the proper GS.
Seneca pilot on IFR flight plan discovers a tower not shown on chart upon breaking out of clouds.
A DHC2 beaver pilot had aircraft damage bent float struts when his engine failed due to water in the carb float bowl. Overwater op float plane.
Aircraft equip problem. Lost communication. Reporter pilot took off; lost communication receiver; flew nonstandard pattern and returned to land. Atc faults pilot for procedures.

Altdev. Xing restr not met. Pf; captain; inexperienced on glass and failed to set VNAV for meeting XING restr. Fo was off frequency on the pa and when returning in the loop captain briefed the clearance. Fo failed to xchk modes.
show: 1996-07 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Cruise

text: An acr ltt had to search a pax's bag when the flight attendant thought that he said 'bomb' when he meant 'bag.' the pax had a hvy spanish accent.

Nmac on approach. Reporter FLC overshot the ctrline on parallel runway; PF; captain; apparently fixated on other runway and came in conflict with aircraft on approach to the parallel. Tcasii and tower alerted reporter FLC to the dev. They corrected back to the clred runway.
Heli pilot on scene departure of ems mission has nmac with an unlighted tower at his 150 ft alt. Fortunately his nightsun lit the tower as he scanned with it so he was able to avoid the tower.

During final approach; PF; FO; held an extra 10 kts of airspd in anticipation of a possible gar. Flc rptrs claim that the approach was very stable. An aci on board took exception and told them that the approach was unstable because of the excess airspd. Argument ensued and aci threatened violations.
Aircraft equip problem. Fuel gauge error. Flc believes aircraft has fuel leak and diverts to near airport for landing. Gauge error detected on post flight inspection.
Aircraft equip problem. Landing gear indicator. Tower fly-by showed gear down; tower declared emer and landing was uneventful.

Questionable landing clearance. Reporter doesn't say if they did or did not have clearance to land; but they landed and apparently nothing was said. Except tower asked them their position when they called on the GND. But; at an airport like ewr that wouldn't be unusual.
Aircraft equip problem. Inverter failure caused smoke in aircraft. Emer.
Maintenance deferred a nondeferrable item; VOR needle off by 10 degrees. Flc assumed that maintenance knew what was correct; but later found out that it was illegal to defer the item.

An acr FLC on the loc to runway 13R finds another acr attempting to join them after their controller's radio fails and they respond to their tcasii's RA twice as the other acr's controller clbs his traffic along with the reporter.
A hot air balloon landed in a cul-de-sac after becoming becalmed over a residential area.
Flc didn't have appropriate stars; sids; or approach plates for dest airport. Acr procedures of providing approach chart changes without a chklist set up the FLC missing their pubs.
Aircraft equip problem. Brake lockup. Reporter GND looped at approx 20 kts on landing rollout. Possible pilot brake application problem.
show: 1996-07 · Other Runway Or Taxiway Excursion · Landing

text: Another aircraft on descent into reporter's departure airport; misunderstood his clred alt and was dsnding into reporter's alt. Reporter FLC saw the traffic and followed tcasii RA to avoid other aircraft. Controller clarified with other aircraft their alt assignment.

Inflt weather encounter; severe turb. Injuries. Captain thought he could penetrate a cirri line; but was closed in once going through it and experienced severe turb. Reporter FO was unhappy with the decision; but didn't advocate strongly.
D8 FLC fails to contact tower. Lands without clearance.

Flc of a LR25 circled to land on the wrong runway after completing a VOR approach resulting in the tower requesting a gar due to two falcon jets being towed on the runway they were attempting to land on.
Mooney 231 pilot fails to carry pilot certificate or medical certificate with him. Customs inspector cites pilot with notice of violation (warning).
Mlg FLC responds to descent clearance. Controller queries second aircraft as to why they are not dsnding. Similar sounding call signs.
show: 1996-07 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: An acr B727-200 crew flew through its descent alt on a STAR. Error admitted.
Flc dev. Non adherence to ATC clearance. Error admitted in the failure to xchk VOR DME information for position regarding the alt XING restr.
An acr MD80; super 80 FLC lost the fluid in the left hyd sys after landing and the right hyd sys pressure went to '0.' the FLC stopped the aircraft on the taxiway using brake accumulator pressure.
Non IFR rated pvt pilot initiates an ILS into sba under an IFR flight plan. Imc in VFR flight was the reality with the fars in mind.
show: 1996-07 · Inflight: VFR In IMC · Initial Approach

text: Flc at cle attempted departure on runway 28 instead of runway 23L. Flc states that the signage at the intersection of runway 23L-right and runway 28 at taxiway j is confusing. Neither crew member had operated at cle prior to the incident.
Sma pilot; training in progress; fails to adhere to ATC clearance. Ta given but pilot starts a heading track to dev that would have created a potential conflict ltss.
Low time pvt pilot performs an unauthorized landing at a mil field. Prox of multiple arpts; had a problem with airport visual signature. Approach to wrong airport.
show: 1996-07 · Procedural: Landing Without Clearance · Initial Approach

text: Navigation error occurs when corporate pilot fails to program his gps correctly. Error admitted in pilot behavior complacency. Also failed to utilize associated vors for navigation chk. Non adherence to ATC in a heading track dev.
show: 1996-07 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: Sma pilot runs into icing on clbout. Turns aircraft as he advises ARTCC radar controller of his intent to descend out of the icing.

Flc in mdt missed reading the NOTAM published on their dispatch papers and thus failed to self announce on the correct frequency at their non tower airport CTAF. Nmac occurs with other arrival traffic. Error admitted by FO.
Nmac btwn a C180 skywagon on pipeline patrol and an ultralight near a non tower airport unicom. See and avoid utilized at the last moment. Evasive action turn.

Acr flight experiences heading track dev during a clearance interp problem with a clearance readback improperly performed. Alert approach controller sees impending conflict and issues a new clearance for acr. Controller cites antiquated radio communication equip at socal approach as being difficult to use.

Heading dev. Assigned heading was 060 degrees; but PF; FO; thought the heading was 100 degrees; asked the captain; pnf; to confirm the heading; and the captain set 060 degrees on the heading bug. Controller intervened and told them the assigned heading was 100 degrees and because of the heading dev; they conflicted with another aircraft. Flc attributes fatigue to the lack of vigilance and FLC coord.

Artcc radar controller misspoke alt for acr x to maintain on the pye arrival; then pointed out traffic to the acr. The acr said he was looking and started a slow descent and separation was lost with aircraft b.
Tcasii alerts A320 FLC to an impending potential conflict with dsnding opposite-direction traffic. Traffic was about to perform descent through occupied alt. Evasive action turn level off.

Artcc controller complaint on aircraft not being rerouted inbound to iad to miss level 3 and 4 tstms on the normal routing. Central flow control and the ARTCC tmu had sufficient information on the weather; but did not take any action until the radar controllers at zbw and at zny made several complaints. Reporter indicates a UCR was filed on this safety issue.
Controller turns traffic on xwind with traffic entering downwind opposite direction.
A cpr hawker 800 had ltss with an acr jetstream. Hawker error admitted.
An acr MD88 captain thinks that the ATC sys is overloaded at times; especially at night and in the weather.
A flight instructor in a C172 reports that his student clbed into the N90 class b airspace without clearance. Training in progress.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Climb
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: An acr B737-400 FO scraped the belly on landing. Aircraft damage fuselage skin; 2 antennas. Error admitted.
An sma pilot entered class d airspace without clearance. Error admitted. He was naving around a flight of ultralight aircraft.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Cruise
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: An sma pilot appeared to fly too close to several hot air balloons that were engaged in a special interest activity hot air balloon meet.
A hot air balloon pilot hits pwrlines on takeoff at a special interest activity hot air balloon meet.

Clearance confusion with foreign controller. Flc directed by controller to 008W to hold. Flc thought the sivir at 46N 008W was the point; but it wasn't. Controller intervened when they had passed the holding fix point and FLC returned to clred fix; but then; before reaching it; were clred on rte.
show: 1996-07 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: An acr CL65 crew denied jumpseat access to an aci because of an aircraft equip problem low oxygen pressure. They compounded the problem by not filling the oxygen and not getting a maintenance deferral prior to departure. Error admitted.
An acr hvt freighter blew apart several taxiway signs while attempting to make a tight taxi turn. Taxiing traffic.
Flc of an ltt clbed and turned in response to a tcasii RA and the visual sighting on a DC8 on a visual climb.
Flc of an ltt was instructed to stop their departure climb and level off at a lower alt. A B727 climbing at a lower alt was given a turn by ATC in response to a tcasii RA reported by the pilot.

Approach controller working the n arrival sector saw a DC10 encroach on his airspace and get near to his B737 on an ILS to runway 24R. The DC10 was supposed to be on an ILS runway 25L approach but was off course and below the published alt prior to hunda. Controller got the B737 to accept visual separation after traffic was pointed out and sighted.
Flc of a charter airline failed to get the required 16 hrs of rest after flying more than 8 hrs the previous day due to weather delays.
Pilot of a mooney M20J inadvertently clbed into class c airspace without contact with them. The airport tower she had just departed alerted her to her error.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Climb
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: Pvt pilot testing a mooney 231; model M20K; struck the prop during a gear up landing gar.

Reporter (acr captain) writes about problems that he experienced as a result of ATC procedures during the recent summer olympics. The 3 primary problems cited involved the approach controller's issuance of visual approach clearances during conditions of low visibility in haze; wake turb encounters; and the atct controller's practice of issuing takeoff clearances to a departing aircraft before the preceding aircraft had departed the runway.
Nose landing gear door opened for maintenance; but not closed and locked when dispatched. Md80.

Taxiing into gate; svc truck was parked incorrectly; but markings on pavement appeared to show the truck outside of the line. A driver on baggage loader was watching the taxi in; but didn't indicate any problem. Aircraft wingtip hit the svc truck.
Ltt commuter aircraft did not develop takeoff pwr on left engine. Aircraft taxied off the runway.
A pvt smt got lost while taxiing at slc. Error admitted. The reporter had also started an approach to the wrong runway.
show: 1996-07 · Other Runway Or Taxiway Excursion · Parked

text: A piper warrior failed to maintain its assigned alt while his pax were taking pictures. Error admitted.

Reported situation of departing acr jet overtaking a slower acr B727. Reporter stated the tower controller didn't take into account the slower performance of the B727 before releasing the second jet. Reporter implied a ltss.
Flc of an ltt returned to land after the nose gear would not retract caused by the aircraft towing pin being left in for takeoff.
Flc of a B737-300 failed to follow ATC instructions and turned base leg prior to ATC request causing a loss of separation with a B767 on final for another set of parallel runways.
An acr FLC on an mlg report that they were unable to meet a XING speed restr.
Nmac btwn a B727 climbing out after takeoff and a beechcraft BE200 on a converging course. The B727 took evasive action by climbing in response to tcasii RA and visual sighting of the other aircraft.
Socal tracon controller reports a violation of an alt XING restr that numerous FLC have been missing by dsnding early. This early descent is through an enrte airway e of lax (fuelr intersection).
show: 1996-07 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: Tower controller taxied a cessna citation onto an active runway in front of a piper PA30 taking off causing the PA30 to takeoff prematurely due to its max gross wt. The pilot lowered the aircraft nose to gain more flying speed after clring the citation aircraft.

A pilot reports having been accused of acting in violation of part 135 rules while riding in the right seat of a single pilot ems flight. This reporter was handling radio communication with ATC; but was not auth as a pilot for this op.

Reporter FO had received tower instructions to hold short of parallel taxiway after clring their landing runway. Captain started to cross the parallel; but reporter questioned if they had been clred. The captain stopped; but beyond the hold line just as an aircraft was takeoff roll on that runway. Flc had been on a 7 leg; 11 hr day and reporter attributes lack of hearing instructions to fatigue.
During a high workload departure compounded by weather; this reporter was assigned; but misunderstood the alt assignment. Altdev alt overshot 700 ft.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Climb
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: An experienced commercial pilot taxied across the active runway without a clearance because he did not know that the airport had recently become tower controlled. The reporter stated that he did not get a standard preflt briefing from fss and he did not receive information from the FBO or see any signs regarding the new control tower at the airport. Also; the new tower structure was not highly visible.
A C172 pilot reports an electrical failure and a subsequent landing at a class d airport without a clearance via the tower controller's light signals.
An acr mlg FLC overshot their assigned alt during the departure climb. The error was detected by the pnf and the alt alerter. The PF was distr task trim.

Reporter was on final for runway 18L at new and was unable to get any pwr out of engine to make it to the runway. Aircraft ditched in water approx 200 yds short of the runway. No injuries and some damage to aircraft.

Aircraft equip problem. An erroneous waypoint had been inserted into the FMS by a previous FLC; but when the reporter FLC called up the waypoint; there was no distinction btwn database information or FLC inserted information. Controller had assigned a XING alt restr and repeatedly asked FLC if they would make it. Since the waypoint fix to which they were going was in error; they were misled and were 50 mi off on the fix XING.
show: 1996-07 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: B727 FLC has tcasii RA during arrival and clbs 1500 ft with conflicting traffic staying at 400 ft below during the climb.

These E120 pilot rptrs experienced confusion over the controller's query about their assigned heading. The approach controller assigned a new heading clearance as a result of traffic within 5 NM of this FLC's aircraft. No other explanation was offered.

Artcc radar controller working a combined sector confign attempted handoff on an LR55 to bwi approach control. The automated handoff went to the wrong sector and the ARTCC controller had to change the LR55 alt; but not soon enough to prevent ltss from occurring. Artcc radar controller blames automation for this incident.

Flying club cfii gave some advice via telephone on how to handle a club C172 that had nosewheel shimmy while operating at another airport. Pilot took advice and ended up stalling aircraft on takeoff and collapsing the nose gear and catching wingtip on runway.
show: 1996-07 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: A DC10 FLC declared an emer and returned to land after smelling electrical smoke fumes during their departure climb; at 14000 ft. The FLC had originally delayed departure for maintenance consultation regarding a duct overheat annunciator that was then deferred by maintenance. Follow-up maintenance inspection revealed an unrelated problem of air cycle machine fumes caused by a #1 engine oil leak.

Turbojet air taxi FLC followed what they believed to be the lax runway 25 ILS GS. When the aircraft was at 1200 ft and still 14 NM out; the approach controller intervened. The rpting captain clbed up to the loc mda and continued the approach. This reporter believes that the GS may have shown neutral or level; when the adi had not captured.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Initial Approach
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: Approach controller vectoring a B757 for approach dsnded the aircraft to 6000 ft when he saw a B737 working with adjacent arrival controller appear to leave 6000 ft. On a second scan he saw that the B737 was still at 6000 ft and aircraft were converging; so he clbed the B757 to 7000 ft. The B757 got a tcasii RA to descend; but ignored it as he was already climbing and in the turn the controller had given him. Ltss occurred.
Under guidance by 2 marshallers; aircraft hit portable light pole with minor damage to right wingtip.
Be35 pilot lands gear and flaps up.
An acr MD11 crew responded properly to a false GPWS warning. Altdev. Foreign airspace. Night op. Designated mountainous terrain.
show: 1996-07 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: Cabin attendants reported noise in air-conditioning sys right side of cabin rows 14 to 21.
Aircraft equip problem. Broken gear box bolt caused loss of oil. Engine shutdown and uneventful single engine landing.
An acr MD80 captain apologizes for some unknown misdeed which may include an altdev while he was out of the cockpit.
show: 1996-07 · Other No Specific Anomaly Occurred · Descent

text: Pax (pilot) reports landing on a hwy when the aircraft ran out of fuel. This pilot reports a cylinder intake leak that caused a high fuel burn rate as a result of erroneous leaning of the engine.

A captain reports having left the approach controller's frequency without a handoff. The flight was on vectors for a visual approach in VFR conditions; with the field in sight; and requested further clearance from the tower. The approach controller had become distracted xmitting a clearance given to an aircraft that was still on the GND.
show: 1996-07 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: Taxiway wt limit not clrly defined or noted on airport diagram page. Apparent lack of taxiway lighting alerted FLC to question tower about wt restr.
show: 1996-07 · Other Runway Or Taxiway Excursion · Parked

text: Flight into temporary flight restr area. Reporter heli pilot says that vertigo caused him to descend into the temporary flight restr area and was repeatedly queried by ATC.
Velocity 200RG aircraft lifts off at 75 kts but settles back onto runway. Pilot aborts the takeoff and runs out of runway into fence.
A C560 FO reports failing to begin descent to meet an alt XING restr clearance. The ARTCC radar controller intervened and gave the crew a turn so that they could descend to the assigned alt.
B727 FLC reports inadvertently setting the wrong altimeter. The mistake was discovered on the party line; but late because the crew was already dsnding through the assigned alt.
An SF34 captain reports an nmac that occurred during the departure climb from a class d airport. The other aircraft was a non xponder equipped cessna on a photo shoot mission.
An acr B727 crew overshot its alt on descent. Error admitted. Training in progress.

An acr FLC declared a medical emer; received priority handling; and exceeded 250 kts below 10000 ft; to obtain medical help for an injured flight attendant. After using every means possible to get the flight attendant down onto the GND and with the medical help; the aircraft waited 9 minutes for the jetway in order to enplane the paramedics.
An acr MD80 crew chose to diver land with a sulfur smelling smoke haze in the cabin. Emer declared. Emer crash alert activated.

Flc of an mlg dsnded in response to a tcasii RA and observation of the traffic dsnding toward them. Atc subsequently instructed the reporter and the other aircraft to turn and the other aircraft to stop dsnding and maintain their alt.
An acr wdb leveled off 200 ft high. Aircraft equip problem altimeters did not agree; off by 80 ft. This should be close enough at alt; but slightly out of limits at origin. Error admitted.

Pilot landing his maule aircraft with a 90 degree xwind got caught with a gust of wind on landing rollout and during his corrective maneuver the aircraft nosed over long enough to catch his prop on the GND.
show: 1996-07 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: Nmac reported and evasive turn made to avoid traffic. Approach control reported traffic not painted (on the radar). Flc reported no tcasii visual or aural alert.
Temporarily lost communication with ATC. Controller tried to contact FLC to issue descent clearance; but FLC didn't hear until almost at dest. Late descent.
An acr mlg crew failed to enter a waypoint in their FMC. This caused them to fly 'oveto' direct dvc vice via the prescribed routing. Error admitted.
show: 1996-07 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: Wake turb encounter. Intrail B737-200 of an L1011; 15 DME; B737 hit turb causing rapid rolls left and right with flight attendants thrown around in aircraft. No injuries; but much stress.

Faulty loc and GS signal on captain inst -- both ctred; so captain started descent; thinking he was on the GS. Reporter FO alerted captain that his GS was still deflected full up; but the captain continued dsnding; even when the controller intervened 3 times of low alt alert. After breaking out of clouds; the captain leveled and continued visually.
While performing GND ref maneuvers at 1000 ft; this reporter pilot observed another aircraft at nearly the same alt; turning away from him.
An acr MD80 FO misunderstood his descent clearance and missed his XING alt. Error admitted. Altdev.
An acr MD80 did not accept a reroute clearance because they did not have time to chk their single engine drift-down performance tables. Designated mountainous terrain.

Approach controller was slow in answering and identing a PA28 on flight towards san. Says PA28 flew through sna class c airspace and was fast approach san class b airspace when idented. Reporter thinks either devious pilot or confusion over airspace identifiers.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Cruise
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: Captain of a sikorsky heli S58T took evasive action by making a vert climb and sidestepping to avoid a cessna 150 on final right over the top of the area in which the reporter had been clred by the tower for takeoff. Nmac.
An acr mlg crew flew an aircraft with an improperly rigged pax seat. The MEL was improperly interpreted and applied. Error admitted.
A hot air balloon pilot flew into bad airspace without prior clearance.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Cruise
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: Landing runway changed when FLC was close in to airport and FMS reprogrammed accordingly. Atc instructed FLC to fly a pattern which would not interfere with the area noise abatement which in turn kept aircraft high and close in. As a result spoilers; flaps and gear were deployed to slow and descend; but the spoilers were forgotten as was the landing chklist. Consequently; airspd degraded; autothrottles responded which were then turned off in order to not overspd the flaps and minimum approach speed maintained.

An MD80 captain reports intercepting the wrong radial on the thundr transition of the FLL7 departure. The FO had set up the radios prior to departure and the captain failed to verify that the correct course had been set. Early morning sun on the digital display; and mechanical problems; compounded the crew's failure to recognize this mistake.
show: 1996-07 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: An acr FLC reports having followed a pilot's discretion clearance after receiving an amended clearance to descend from FL390 to FL370. The crew even read back the clearance including the earlier pilot's discretion to FL240. At FL340; the controller intervened.

Approach controller was questioned about prox of traffic by a DHC8 FLC who was getting a tcasii RA. Controller advised FLC nearest traffic was 600 ft below. Flc turned off their tcasii for safety reasons.
Aircraft equip problem. Engine cowling came off inflt. Dispatcher notified the FLC before landing at dest.

A acr FK10 captain reports receiving an old field report which was not only inaccurate; but also contained minimal information regarding ramp construction. The reporter cited concerns about legal pilot briefing requirements of his airline (primarily 'left' notams) versus the easy accessibility of the information required to be presented to the pilots.

A chartered freight FLC discover enrte that there was an error in the flight plan and the rte was approx 500 NM longer than planned. The FLC diverts to a nearby airport for additional fuel before completing the flight.
Flc of an mlg report a XING restr dev that resulted from an FMS waypoint bypass. The FMS was not backed up with raw data or chked against a descent profile formula. Altdev alt undershot XING restr.

Gnd observer report regarding a spi who was lost on a xcountry flight and night flying with no night experience. Spi in communication with his instructor via VHF. Reporter; also an instructor suggested contacting approach control and gave the frequency.

Land without clearance. Reporter told to keep speed up on approach and clred for the approach. Flc believed they had been clred to land; but never went to tower frequency. The FLC was using nonstandard chklist; and instead of using the mechanical chklist last 2 items for approach clearance and landing clearance; they were using autothrottles and autoplt.
Sma pilot using hand drawn approach chart makes a low circling approach. Faa inspector observer questions his procedures.
Be95 instructor with student has engine failure due to switch to wrong tank. Forced landing on airport.

Aircraft equip problem. Landing gear handle would not move to retract position. Flc troubleshooting the problem idented the 12G microswitch in the nose gear as the cause. They decided to land hard enough to make the switch function correctly; which they did and then continued on to dest. After landing reporter's company advised them they were in non compliance with the maintenance manual and faced disciplinary action.
Approach and associate controllers at the pom sector in lax tracon observed an MD80 on the ILS runway 25L approach bust the XING alt at fuelr intersection.
show: 1996-07 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Initial Approach
cat: Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit

text: Lcl controller attitude and poor handling create problem for instructor with student pilot.
An FK10 captain reports a bird strike.

Wake encounter. Controller reporter received report from pilot of an E120 saying a wake almost rolled over the aircraft. Following a B757 in prescribed in trail spacing; 5 mi; controller slowed the reporter aircraft as well as approved a higher alt.

Acr jet on civet arrival clred for the ILS runway 25L approach. Fo flying intercepted the GS and dsnded per the GS indications. Fo didn't have approach plate out and asked captain about alts and was told just follow the GS. Approach controller chastised the FLC for XING fuelr 500 ft low. Captain of first B737 received a tcasii on the other aircraft and followed it; then questioned the controller on the vector; and felt he could have done a better job of spacing his aircraft.

Vfr PA28 turning base to final and following another aircraft spotted a twin aircraft in close prox and dsnded and turned to avoid the twin aircraft. Reporter alleges the tower lcl controller lost the situational awareness of his traffic.

A corporate jet FO says ATC turned his aircraft and clbed him to 17000 ft. Passing 9400 ft ATC issued traffic at 12 o'clock at 9000 ft. Reporter saw acr aircraft pass below his aircraft in close prox. Reporter aircraft not tcasii equipped; but reporter is going to petition for it now.
Flc of a cessna citation jet overshot descent assigned alt due to copying the wrong alt resulting in ATC intervention.
Conflict occurs when mlg is told to maintain visual separation from an MD80 on departure from lax.
B727 FLC hits sign when turning off the runway onto ramp area at night.
Captain of an mdt turboprop scheduled pax operations flew several flights when her first class medical certificate had expired.
Flc of a wdb failed to turn as required on departure causing ATC to intervene. Error was caused by the flying FO not activating the navigation function on the FMS.

Dc9 is evaced when a pax releases pepper spray either intentionally or unintentionally.

An acr B757 pilot reports sport parachutists dropping unannounced on his rte of flight. Drop aircraft pltdev; there was no 'jumpers away' from the drop aircraft; although ARTCC had been notified of the intent to drop parachutes.
B727 cargo crew declared emer when smoke and fumes entered the cockpit.
Ltt late starting descent on ILS approach caused conflict with a mooney.

text: B737-500 FL370 on sadde STAR; derbb transition; balancing fuel; has flameout #2 engine. Maintenance had replaced xfeed valve earlier in the day. Crew declared emer and began a descent and was able to restart engine at lower level. Continued to lax and landed normally.
Acr mlg 100 mi ne bna; leveling FL280; e of line of tstms; encountered strong updraft and ballooned to 28280 ft. Returned immediately to FL280.

B747-200 FL390 enrte nrt. So balancing fuel. Distr by captain leaving cockpit turned off #3 fuel boost pump with the xfeed closed resulting in flameout of #3 engine. Attempted relight but requested clearance to descend and had a successful relight at FL250. Landed normal nrt.

Aa5 tiger on routine pleasure flight with pax encountered light to moderate turb causing pax to panic. Pilot had difficulty controlling aircraft and declared emer to land dkb airport. Noticed pax leg on rudder pedal and asked him to relax resulting in normal landing and end of control problem.
Flc of a B737-200 are confused about ATC vector instructions provided for necessary traffic spacing at high alt and not being advised of the reason until level at 3000 ft above the other traffic.

Acr maintenance installed the wrong thrust reverser on a DC9-30 aircraft and found their mistake and re-rted the aircraft back to maintenance for change to the correct part within 48 hrs. However; the aircraft did carry pax back to the maintenance base after the company found out about the wrong part. Facts available indicated that the wrong part operated satisfactorily. The mechs involved had 23; 30; 25 and 25 yrs experience respectively.

Acr wdb holding at lendy intersection FL200; alt hold switch tripped off resulting in altdev of 300 ft; got 19700 ft. Fo; PF; corrected back to assigned alt. Captain and so discussing fuel remaining with dispatch.

Tower just recently went from FAA control to a contract tower. Reporter says too much traffic for controller to safely handle.
The aircraft after takeoff remained in the GND mode. The crew returned and landed. The reporter feels there should be an abnormal chklist to accommodate that event.
Unauthorized approach and landing when airport weather minimums for alternate airport go below legal limits for approach.

A320 aircraft during climb the mcdu indicated 'chk aircraft position.' FLC chked navigation computers and noted that all 3 irs devs were 99 pt 9 mi in error. B727 flight left stl with the wrong aircraft logbook.

The pilot made a heading correction to return to track to compensate for a scalloping VOR. He then became occupied with a traffic watch. A few minutes later he noticed a full scale deflection on the cdi. As the reporter started to correct the controller gave a new heading for course correction.

Flight attendant from a foreign country rides the jump seat in the cockpit. Captain fails to chk credentials of the jump seat rider and fails to discover the rider is not a pilot.
Flc suspects nose gear tire blows during takeoff from pop; so ask CFR to stand by during landing at jfk.
B767-300 returns to land at jfk when #2 generator has a fault. Engine is shut down because it starts to surge. Emer declared.
F100 aircraft during climb FLC forgot to reset altimeter at FL180 and ended up 400 ft high at leveloff. Controller intervened and they corrected both the altimeter setting and their alt.

During a inst training flight in a C152; the code c xponder was unusable on several codes; the #2 VOR ident would not work and the directional gyroscope became inop causing the instructor to ask for a no gyroscope approach! Atc provided a flight assist to a successful landing.

text: Atx pilot of an smt twin found ceiling lower than the latest current weather reported by a manned observation which is delayed up to 30 minutes before given to fss for pilot briefings.
An auth inspector found when making an annual inspection of a C310 that an stc for different induction air filters had not been recorded with the FAA or shown in the aircraft logbooks.

B727 aircraft had compressor stall on #3 engine just after rotation. Throttle was retarded to idle; an emer was declared and FLC returned to land. After landing the cargo door came open and some baggage dropped on the runway.
Nmac btwn an ltt turboprop acr making a VFR clbout from a non controlled airport; going through 4000 ft; and 2 mil fighter A4 aircraft; dsnding to an adjacent nearby mil airport approx 4 mi away.
B727 involved in a critical GND conflict when it enters the runway while an sma takes off from the opposite end of the runway.
Captain of an MD88 failed to hold short of runway as instructed in taxi instructions causing tower to intervene in order to clear runway.

Pvt pilot of a cessna 177 struck a tv antenna mounted on a 2 story house off the approach end of runway 26 at lodi; ca. A normal landing was made with no damage to the aircraft. The reporter heard a noise in the engine compartment area and thought the engine may have 'blown!'

Taxiway lighting out caused FLC to become disoriented on their taxiway position. Night; reflection of airport lights on wet pavement contributed. Flc stopped aircraft and were towed into gate without any damage.

text: An instructor cabin attendant reports that her cockpit crew taxied with pax standing and that there is an aircraft equip problem the ATR42 can leak water into the cabin during rainstorms on the GND. There is no water leakage in the air.
A B757 was dispatched with improper placards on deferred items.

Captain of a SF340 while taxiing for takeoff failed to hold short of the runway and taxied on to it before being clred to do so. Tower provided supplemental instructions for repositioning the aircraft for takeoff.
Pilot of an smt taxied onto runway and started takeoff without clearance resulting in tower intervention to abort the takeoff and clear the runway at once.

Acr DHC8 landed runway 09 and told to clear at third taxiway and hold short of the parallel taxiway. Captain reporter did not clear the runway as he felt he could not comply with the hold short of parallel instructions and allow tower to clear other aircraft for takeoff. Reporter questions competency of the non federal tower controllers.

Flc of a DC9 declared an emer and dsnded due to smoke in the cabin. Since they were dsnding to their dest they continued at a lower alt unpressurized and landed at dest within 17 minutes. The smoke stopped when the left 'pack' was turned off. There was no fire or injuries to pax or crew.

Beech 1900 aircraft. Prior to departure FLC gave pax briefing including the exit row seating and; if anyone wanted to be moved or couldn't open an exit; they should be reseated. Apparently one of the pax tried to get flcs attention that someone who couldn't speak english was seated in an exit row and should be moved. Flc looked back into the cabin but didn't see the pax who was attempting to get their attention. Pax told them that they had violated fars.

A320 depart runway 25R lax. Commuter express depart runway 25L to maintain visual on traffic off runway 25R. A320 got tcasii RA alert and saw traffic 7-8 o'clock commuter express. Reduced climb rate for further separation. No comment from controller.

Pilot of a single pilot atx cargo cessna 401 lost all electrical pwr during cruise in IMC resulting in the loss of all radios and consequently; air-GND communications. The reporter used a hand held cellular phone to contact ATC center and then subsequently; the dest approach facility. He declared an emer to receive priority handling and landed safely.
B737 departed phl without IFR clearance. Long duty day previous with a short layover. Departure control issued xponder code and clearance.

Cl65 commuter aircraft climbing through 1000 ft got a thrust reverser unlock warning message. Chklist accomplished and still had warning. Fo advised chklist inferred ok to continue but captain elected to shut down engine and return to tlh. Emer was declared.
Flc of a DC8-63 failed to contact the tower and receive landing clearance after being clred for the approach by approach control.
N265. Improperly programmed gps caused navigation error and FLC missed a heading change. Atc intervened and provided vector on course.
show: 1996-10 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: Controller training in progress in tower. Lcl controller clred a C172 for takeoff on RENO2 SID and shortly thereafter clred a B737 for takeoff on a mustang 4 SID. B737 was observed by departure controller overtaking the C172 se the airport and departure controller turned the B737 and issued traffic to him. B737 sighted traffic and was clred to maintain visual separation; but not before a sys error occurred.
Pilot of a cessna 182 operated in less than VFR during a contact approach.

Captain of UH60 blackhawk heli took evasive action by lifting up and out of the way while taxiing to avoid an oncoming cessna 210 taxiing at a high rate of speed. Even though the reporter did not get tower clearance for the lift off; he felt that evasive action was necessary in the interest of safety.

Light aircraft encountering turb. Captain reporter took over flying from the flying FO. Captain disconnected both autoplt and autothrottles; dsnded to 31000 ft; reconnected autoplt; aircraft leveled and captain gave the flying back to FO. Fo was not aware that the autothrottles were still disconnected until stick shaker went off indicating approach to a stall. Both FLC were distracted with other things at the time.
Pilot of a cessna 402 was alerted on short final that his landing gear was not down so he recycled the gear switch and extended the gear for a safe landing.

Pilot of a piper PA31-350 turned to avoid parachutist falling from an aircraft nearby at night. The jumpers; as well as the jump aircraft; had the required lights on for night operations. Atc had been notified; but had not passed on the information to the reporter during his contacts! Close encounter btwn the jump aircraft; parachutist and reporter.

A new television or radio tower has been constructed near the final approach path of runway 8 at hvc; without the airport advisory board's previous knowledge or approval. A reporter estimates that the tower is 200-300 ft AGL and states that it comes within 150 ft of the aircraft's right wingtip while the aircraft is on final approach and following the PAPI to runway 8.

Acr on downwind vector runway 24R ILS given left turn to 060 degrees thought should be 160 degrees. Start right turn and the FO questioned the turn. Controller issued immediate left turn at the same time had tcasii ta alert. Controller was very busy and overloaded. Replaced about 1 min after the incident.

Approach controller used wrong call sign while vectoring a B737 to intercept the loc final approach course and the aircraft overshot the final approach and had ltss from a DO328 on a vector to follow the B737.

Flight instructor in an sma sel gives a simulated engine failure to a student pilot during takeoff roll resulting in the complete engine stoppage. Even though the aircraft became airborne a few ft; it was stopped safely on the runway and then pushed off on to the side.
A DC9 was dsnded 800 ft below its assigned alt. The FLC had mistaken a clearance for another company airplane (similar flight number) as their clearance to descend. The center controller intervened.

text: Pilot of a mooney M20C made an off airport forced landing when he ran out of fuel. Pilot indicates he should have landed at the original destination.
Flc of an ltt turbo prop aborted takeoff due to the low oil pressure light coming on during takeoff roll. The cause was found to be low oil quantity.

Flc of a B737-100 lost communication during a STAR arrival resulting in not following the alt descent profile depicted. Subsequently; re-established communication over dest airport and was given another arrival rte with no further communication problems.

Similar call signs caused miscom btwn ATC and FLC. Flc responded to another aircraft call sign; ATC missed the wrong aircraft reading back descent clearance.

text: An acr FLC performs a high speed reject when the B737-300 does not rotate. Later maintenance finds that a bearing in the elevator ctring mechanism had failed. B737-300.
Flc failed to descend in time to make a XING restr on a STAR arrival.
An acr B777 received and responded to a tcasii RA to descend and saw a VFR BE20 pass 200 ft directly overhead. The BE20 apparently never saw the B777 and controller credits the tcasii for a save.
Acr on departure mco; failed to maintain 250 kias as specified in the pdc. Departure controller called the error.
B747 cargo departed sdf without aircraft logbook on board. Initial decision to continue to anc; but dispatch sent acars message to return to sdf.

Ce172k landed runway 15; clred to exit on high speed; hold short runway 15L; remain on this frequency. Was distr by request to remain on frequency and did not hold short. Saw aircraft starting takeoff roll and expedited across without clearance.

During an inst training flight the wrong altimeter setting was made causing a low alt readout to ATC. In addition; the mode c alt readout seems to differ to that of the aircraft altimeter in some instances according to ATC feedback.

Md80 aircraft during descent failed to level at newly assigned alt and came in conflict with another aircraft which was climbing and got tcasii warning. Captain was flying and FO was off frequency communication with his acr. Atc issued a new alt clearance to reporter who read it back properly; but failed to level until ATC intervened. Though reporter captain saw tcasii target; he didn't say anything to ATC.
Captain of a lear 25D became distr and failed to descend to the assigned XING alt. This resulted in ATC intervention; who gave vectors for maintaining appropriate separation with other traffic.
Galley fire on a B727-200 during high alt cruise caused by napkins laying in a hot oven caused the fire which was put out by the so and cabin attendant.

Approach controller vectoring a DC10 inbound over the mountains and dsnding him to the mva; to follow a DCH8; discovered that the azimuth on his radar was 30 degrees off. Maintenance was doing some uncoord fine tuning of the radar and reporter concerned he may have put the DC10 too close to terrain and the DHC8.
Pvt pilot of a piper PA34 crossed an active runway without auth after clring active runway after landing.

Dc9-30 attempted approach on runway 28R no GS. Weather much worse than reported. Made gar and made second approach on runway 28L all aids operational. Land ok. No update on atis or that GS was out on runway 28R.
An atx cargo cessna 208 caravan taxied onto a runway while another aircraft was apching for landing. Nmac. Error admitted. Non tower airport unicom. Evasive action stop taxi.
A C172 pilot had to return land when his engine started acting up. Emer declared. Aircraft equip problem spark plug insulators breaking down.

Instructor pilot and student in a C152 doing touch and goes were sequenced to follow a PA23 inbound over the 'city' for landing. They spotted the wrong aircraft and cut in front of the PA23 they were to follow. The lcl controller told the C152 to make a 360 degree turn to follow the PA23 and the aircraft had an nmac. Both aircraft were sent around and new controller took over the lcl control position.

Artcc controller clred an acr B727 to descend and cross lamma intersection at 15000 ft on STAR into mco. The B727 was following a B767 on the STAR that had a cargo door problem and was restr to 270 kts. The B727 misinterp alt XING restr and dsnded below 15000 ft. Controller reporter saw mode c readout and alt infraction at 13400 ft and tried to stop the B727 at 13000 ft. Aircraft overshot that alt and ltss occurred.

Atr42 aircraft during clbout from airport was observed to be trailing smoke. Reporter captain returned to airport; but was unable to determine the smoke source.
A mlg transport was dispatched with 1 crew personal breathing deferred inop.

Mdt aircraft possible wt and bal error after aircraft parked; reporter captain noted that the nose rose as pax were deplaning. Reporter suspects the wt was not properly calculated; the nose came up when parked; the nosewheel swung 90 degrees which in turn broke the steering linkage.

Ltss btwn a dsnding BE35 and a E120 level at 6000 ft. The dsnding aircraft was on approach frequency and the E120 was on the center frequency. Reporter saw the potential conflict but did nothing to avert the situation until told to descend the E120 to 5000 ft by the approach controller. The instruction was issued but was not acknowledged. The BE35 was observed in a climb mode. The E120 received an RA. The FLC said they were at 7000 ft but the mode c showed 6000 ft.

Flc of ltt commuter aircraft on departure reports nmac with inbound C337. Reporter claims traffic was not issued by the lcl control. Fo sighted the C337 at one fourth mi. Reporter stopped SID turn and increased pitch for more separation. Supvr told reporter that the controller had both the aircraft in sight and didn't feel there was a conflict.

Flc of a jetstream 3100 heard a loud thump during initial climb after takeoff and returned to land thinking it was probably a bird strike. However; it was one of the engine cowlings coming off the aircraft and striking the horiz stabilizer which caused a slight erratic jerk of the control yoke.
Flc of a wdb failed to turn as depicted on the SID departure clearance resulting in ATC intervention and vectors given to them to get back on published course.

After the landing; FLC had second thoughts about making the approach with those minimums.

Artcc radar controller vectoring an acr DC9 for traffic took a handoff on an acr B727 that was on a converging course at the same alt and did not notice the potential conflict ltss situation developing btwn the 2 aircraft. The B727 received a tcasii RA and advised the controller he was dsnding.
Air taxi cargo flight departs with weather below minimums. Flc hurrying to beat deteriorating weather.

Instructor with IFR student has nmac with another aircraft flying close to the non tower airport at which they were making an approach. Using full throttle they sidestepped the aircraft and executed a low approach.
Mlg FLC fails to comply with company procedures; fails to make logbook entry when fuel gauge malfunctions. Reporter believes mech to be company employee.

Casa 212 on civilian parachute jump op. Jumpmaster failed to order parachutist to jump over release point. One tandem pair ended landing 8 pt 5 mi from target on cape canaveral space shuttle landing strip. Arrested by base security.

text: L1011 on sinca 3 STAR failed to make 12000 ft XING at canuk. Fms had chked within 2 mi when programmed at fll; but now indicated 26 mi to canuk. Ztl advised flight was over canuk and issued 360 degree turn to get down. Chking VOR DME confirmed error in FMS. Reset navigation and waypoint page on FMS and it immediately corrected.

text: Cpr jet clred for civet 1 STAR lax. Captain covered civet procedure with his charts manual and inadvertently set FMS up for the downe 4 arrival. Requested clearance to start descent and advised already clred for the civet 1 STAR. Realized error and advised center could not make the restr. Unable on next XING restr and clred to descend to 10000 ft. Error admitted to the controller and on landing lax discussed incident with supvr. No conflict or problem resulted.

text: Nmac btwn an light on a noise abatement departure climb; who stopped climbing and dsnded in response to a tcasii RA; and an unknown aircraft that just popped up on ATC radar. The see and avoid is still applicable since another aircraft could pop up illegally at any time and turn on its xponder.
Captain of an mlg failed to maintain approach descent alt during final for a visual approach and crossed the required fix 600 ft low.
show: 1996-12 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: An acr FLC has the audio entertainment sys wiring short out; with smoke and fumes; behind the window frame molding in the vicinity of rows 25 and 26 on the left hand side of the aircraft. They declared an emer and were vectored and dsnded to the nearest available airport where the pax were deplaned at the gate because the smoke and fumes had dissipated. B757-200.
Both ILS receivers on an acr mlg failed to align themselves properly. The tracon approach controller intervened.
show: 1996-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: Acr mlg on the gorman 1 SID was clred direct gmn maintain 15000 ft. Zla gave a vector of 330 degrees and FLC thought clred to climb FL330. Controller very busy and FLC unable to confirm climb to FL330. Before contact made with zla had reached 15600 ft. Clearance was to maintain 15000 ft. When clear of traffic 5 mi clred to climb to FL330 and direct shafter.
Inbound dsnding DC9 on visual approach has nmac with a cessna who was supposed to be over the shoreline. Overwater op. Non radar approach procedure.

Pilot of a BE55 experienced a loss of communication while departing pwk on an IFR flight plan. The mike jack receptacle fell off the pedestal interior; disconnecting the mike jack; which prevented voice modulation. The reporter was unable to retrieve the receptacle while flying; so he turned back toward a non tower airport and thereby received ATC attention and vectors through carrier wave xmission acknowledgment.
A hot air balloon ride pilot had to fly low to find a suitable landing site.
Flc confusion over clearance interp and possible altdev alt overshot in descent.

Flc of a B727 took the appropriate escape maneuver by stopping their descent and climbing in response to a GPWS warning. Even though the aircraft was above the mva; the rate of descent and high rising terrain in front of their aircraft could have caused this warning.

Pilot of a C172 discovered that the baggage door was open during postflt inspection of the aircraft. Reporter believes that it was locked prior to takeoff but must have opened inflt while doing stalls and other air work.
Takeoff aborted twice in an AT72. Master caution aircraft confign warning. Pic had thought it was a cabin attendant call on first event. Had heard auditory signal.

An acr mdt jet on the minks 1 arrival received a tcasii RA and dsnded out of his assigned alt over somto intersection and saw a cpr falcon jet pass overhead in close prox. Falcon jet was also in a descent. No traffic information given by approach controller.

Instructor pilot of a student training flight took over aircraft control from the trainee to assure that the class c airspace was not penetrated during climb out from an underlying unctled airport. With the latest altimeter setting; the penetration was only missed by 50 ft.
show: 1996-12 · Other No Specific Anomaly Occurred · Cruise

text: Flc interp of pdc leads them into a heading track position altdev. Alt overshot in climb. A case of clearance interp clearance expected.
B737-300 FLC failed to note routing change on pdc and enrte didn't comply with clearance. Atc intervened; corrected routing and FLC examined pdc further seeing their error.
show: 1996-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: B737 aircraft. After takeoff; the FLC was unable to raise the landing gear. Chklists were completed; company notified; and decision was made to return and land. Flc was vectored immediately back to the ILS; a discrete tower frequency was assigned. Flc very busy loading in new approach into FMC; chklists; etc; and forgot to obtain landing clearance from tower. Were advised after landing.

Sf340 FO finds aircraft damaged during morning preflt inspection. Aircraft had been flown in the night before and FLC had difficulty in maintaining proper cabin pressure. Tug found at the previous departure airport that was determined to be the cause of the damage.

Pilot of a piper PA23C was met by a gov heli upon landing back at their departure airport after a non stop photo flight below the united states adiz boundary. When 100 mi s of key west; FL; communications were lost with center while they dsnded to take photos and was not re-established until reaching a few mi s of the adiz. This caused united states gov officials to not fully know where the flight had gone or its purpose until after the aircraft had landed and could be chked.
show: 1996-12 · Other Airspace Violation Entry or Exit · Cruise
